Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:10:1.english: He violates [the prohibition of] “before the blind” - For it enters the mind of the borrower to deny [the loan].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:10:2.hebrew: קללה - כשתובעו, וזה כופר, הכל מקללין אותו ואומרין שהוא דובר על צדיק עתק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:10:2.english: A curse - When [the lender] claims [the money] from him and [the borrower] denies [it], everyone curses him and says that he is speaking arrogantly against a righteous person.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:11:1.english: And he will forget - He will forget my loan, and I will bring a curse upon myself.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:12:1.english: Cry out - In the earthly court.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:12:2.english: And they are not answered - For they brought [it] upon themselves.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:12:3.english: Acquires a master for himself - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:13:1.hebrew: תולה מעותיו בנכרי - אומר: מעות שאני משתמש בהן של פלוני נכרי הם, שלא להשביע עצמו; ופעמים שהנכרי שומע, ומעמיד עדים, ותובעו בדיניהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:13:1.english: Attributes his money to a gentile - [He] says, "The money that I am using belongs to so-and-so, a gentile," so as not to make himself [appear] wealthy; and sometimes the gentile hears [of this], sets up witnesses, and sues him under their laws.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:1.english: One who hires artisans, and they deceived one another - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:2.hebrew: שכר את החמר או את הקדר להביא פרייפרין וחלילין - קדר — בעל קרון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:2.english: [If] one hired a donkey driver or a kadar to bring canopy poles and flutes - Kadar [means] a wagon owner.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:3.english: Piryafarin - Planed and fine [pieces of] wood to make a canopy for himself.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:4.english: Flutes for a bride - To gladden the groom and bride.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:5.english: Or for the dead - To lament.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:6.hebrew: משרה - רויי"ש, מים ששורין בהן קנבוס ופשתן כשהן בגבעולין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:6.english: Retting tub - [Old French:] rois; water in which hemp and flax are soaked while they are in [their] stalks.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:7.hebrew: מקום שאין אדם - שאינו מוצא פועלין לשכור, והפשתן אבד, והוא סמך עליהן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:7.english: A place where there is no person - [Meaning] that he cannot find laborers to hire, and the flax is being ruined, and he had relied upon them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:8.hebrew: שוכר עליהם - בני אדם ביוקר, ועליהם לשלם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:8.english: He may hire at their expense - [He may hire] people at a high price, and it is upon them to pay.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:15:9.english: Or deceive them - [This] is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:16:1.english: One who hires artisans - To do work by contract for such-and-such [an amount].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:16:2.english: And they reneged - After they did part [of the work].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:16:3.hebrew: ידם על התחתונה - אם הוקרו פועלים ואינו מוצא מי שיגמרנה בשכר שהיה מגיע לאלו על העתיד לעשות, מעכב משכר ממה שעשו כל מה שיצטרך להוציא, עד שתגמר מלאכתו בשכר שפסק עם אלו. ואם הוזלו פועלים וימצא שיגמרנה בפחות, ישום להם מה שעשו ויתן להם מה שפסק — עשו חציה, יתן להם חצי שכרן — ואין יכולים לומר לו: הרי פועלים אחרים תחתינו לגמור מלאכתך, ותן לנו כל שכרינו חוץ ממה שנטלו אלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:16:3.english: They are at a disadvantage - If [the cost of] workers rose and he does not find anyone who will finish it for the wage that would have been due to these [workers] for what remained to be done, he withholds from the wage for what they [already] did whatever he will need to spend, so that his work is finished for the wage he stipulated with these [workers]. And if [the cost of] workers fell and he finds [someone] who will finish it for less, he appraises for them what they did and gives them [according to] what he stipulated — [if] they did half of it, he gives them half their wage — and they cannot say to him, "Here are other workers in our stead to finish your work, and give us all of our wage except for what these [workers] took."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:1.hebrew: כל ימי גריד אחד - הם, ולא דקדקו בדבר לחוש שמא יום אחד יהא ארוך מחבירו או קשה מחבירו, אלא מותר לומר לו: עדור עמי היום הזה של גריד, ואעדור עמך ביום פלוני של גריד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:1.english: All the dry days [are] one - They [are all considered equal], and [the Sages] were not particular about the matter to be concerned lest one day be longer than another or harder than another; rather, it is permitted to say to him: "Hoe with me on this day of the dry [season], and I will hoe with you on such-and-such a day of the dry [season]."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:2.hebrew: גריד - לשון יובש, שהארץ יבשה ואין גשמים יורדין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:2.english: Gerid - [It is] an expression of dryness, for the earth is dry and no rains are falling.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:3.english: And all the rainy days - [are] considered as one.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:1:4.english: But he may not say to him: Plow with me, and I will plow with you in the rainy [season] - For the rainy days are difficult for work in the fields.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:4:1.hebrew: על לא תתן לו - "את כספך לא תתן לו בנשך", עוברין על "בל תתן" ועל "לא תקח" כו'. כל חד וחד מאי דשייך ביה, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:4:1.english: For "You shall not give him" - [This refers to the verse,] "Your money you shall not give him with interest" — they violate "You shall not give" and "Do not take," etc., each and every one [transgressing] that which applies to him, as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:6:1.hebrew: מלוה עובר בכולן - בכל הני דחשיב במתני', דהוא נותן בנשך בשעת הלואה, והוא לוקח בשעת פירעון, והוא לו כנושה כשתובעו ודוחקו, והוא שם עליו נשך בשעת פיסוק התנאי, ונותן מכשול לפני הלוה להעבירו על "לא תשיך לאחיך", שהיא אזהרה ללוה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:6:1.english: The lender violates all of them - [That is,] all of these [prohibitions] that [the Tanna] lists in the Mishnah: for he gives on interest at the time of the loan, and he takes [interest] at the time of repayment, and he is to him like a creditor when he demands [payment from] him and presses him, and he places interest upon him at the time of stipulating the condition, and he places a stumbling block before the borrower to cause him to transgress "You shall not cause your brother to take interest," which is a warning to the borrower.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:7:1.english: [They] lose - As [the Gemara] says in our chapter (daf 71a): they collapse forever.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:8:1.hebrew: לא תהיה לו כנושה - לא תראה בעיניו כנושה בו, שיראה ויבוש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:8:1.english: Do not be to him as a creditor - Do not appear in his eyes as a creditor to him, for he will see [you] and be ashamed.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:9:1.hebrew: לראשנו - לשון נושה, כדמתרגמינן כרשיא. הרי אנו באים באש ובמים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 75b:9:1.english: Over our heads [leroshenu] - [This is] an expression of "creditor" [nosheh], as we translate [into Aramaic] "kerashya" ["like a creditor"]. Behold, we go through fire and through water.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:1.hebrew: השוכר את האומנין - משמע ליה בין בשכיר יום בין בקבלנות, אבל בפרקין דבתר הכי (דף פג.) נקט "פועלים", משום ד"פועלים" לא משמע אלא שכירי יום, דבהכי מיירי, כדאמר התם: "בזמן שאמר להשכים ולהעריב". ורב נמי דקאמר (לקמן בבא מציעא עז.): "פועל יכול לחזור אפילו בחצי היום" — דוקא בשכיר יום איירי ולא בקבלן, כדמוכח בשמעתין, ולכך נקט "פועל" ולא "אומן". וא"ת: דתניא לקמן בשמעתין (שם): "השוכר את הפועל, ובחצי היום שמע שמת לו מת או אחזתו חמה, אם שכיר הוא כו' ואם קבלן הוא כו'", כיון דברייתא מיירי בין בשכיר בין בקבלן, אמאי נקט "פועל"? ה"ל למינקט "אומן" דמשמע תרוייהו. וי"ל דה"ק: אם שכיר הוא — כדאמר "השוכר את הפועל" — נותן לו שכרו, ואם קבלן הוא — כך דינו; ומשום דבעי למתני "ובחצי היום", וחצי היום לא שייך למתני אלא אשכיר יום:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:1.english: "One who hires artisans" - [This term] implies both a day laborer and a contractor, whereas in the next chapter (83a) [the Mishna] uses the term "laborers" [po'alim], because "laborers" implies only day laborers, which is indeed what [that Mishna] is dealing with, as it states there: "When he told them to come early and stay late." And Rav too, who says (below, Bava Metzia 77a): "A laborer [po'el] may retract even in the middle of the day" — he is speaking specifically of a day laborer and not of a contractor, as is evident in our sugya, and therefore he used the term "laborer" and not "artisan" [uman]. And if you ask: Since it is taught in a Baraita below in our sugya (ibid.): "One who hires a laborer, and in the middle of the day he heard that a relative of his died or he was seized by sunstroke: if he is a [day] laborer, etc., and if he is a contractor, etc." — since the Baraita deals with both a [day] laborer and a contractor, why did it use the term "laborer"? It should have used "artisan," which implies both! And one can answer that this is what [the Baraita] means: If he is a [day] laborer — as it just stated, "One who hires a laborer" — he gives him his wages, and if he is a contractor — this is his law; and [it used "laborer"] because it wanted to teach "and in the middle of the day," and "in the middle of the day" is only applicable to teach with respect to a day laborer.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:2.hebrew: את הקרר - בשני רישין, והוא בעל קרון. ולספרים דגרסי קדר, י"ל דלהכי נקט קדר לפי שקדרים רגילין להיות להם קרונות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:2.english: The karar - [Spelled] with two reshes, and he is a wagoner [ba'al karon]. And according to the texts that read kadar [potter], one can say that [the Mishna] specifically mentioned a potter because potters customarily have wagons.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:3.hebrew: פרייפרין - דבר האבוד חשיב לה, שעתה זמנו הוא לעשות:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:15:3.english: Piryafarin - [The Mishnah] considers it a matter involving loss, because now is the time to do it:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:16:1.hebrew: השוכר את האומנין וחזרו בהם ידם על התחתונה - שאם קבלו קמה לקצור בשני סלעים, וקצרו חציה, והוקרו ושוה מה שעתיד לעשות סלע וחצי, וחזרו פועלים — לא יתן להם רק חצי סלע, לפי שיצטרך לתת סלע וחצי לקצור חציה השני; והיינו כר' דוסא. ואם בעה"ב חוזר בו, ידו על התחתונה — פירש בקונטרס: אם הוזלו פועלין, ואין שוה החצי אלא שקל, וחזר בו בעה"ב, יתן להם סלע וחצי, לפי שבחצי הסלע ימצא שיגמרו קצירו. ולא רצה לפרש דידו על התחתונה כשהוקרו פועלין, ויתן להם סלע וחצי על חצי שעשו כמו ששוה עכשיו; שאין זה סברא, כי למה יתן להם בעה"ב יותר ממה שהתנה עמהם, כיון שאין מפסידין בחזרת בעה"ב, ואדרבה יותר מרויחים, שעתה ימצאו שיתנו להם סלע וחצי לקצור חצי קמה, והוא לא היה נותן להם כ"א סלע. וא"ת: דאמר לקמן (בבא מציעא דף עז.): "אמר מר: או יגמרו מלאכתם ויטלו ב' סלעים. פשיטא! לא צריכא דזל עבידתא ואימר בעה"ב ופייסוהו פועלים", והשתא למה חוזר בעה"ב בזה בשביל שהוזל המלאכה? מה מרויח בחזרה? הלא צריך ליתן להם סלע וחצי על מה שעשו! ופועלים נמי למה פייסו, כיון שאין מפסידים כלום? וי"ל: דבעה"ב חוזר מחמת שנאה שהיתה קטטה ביניהם, ופועלים פייסו שלא יצטרכו לחפש ולמצוא מקום להשתכר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:16:1.english: One who hires artisans and they reneged, they are at a disadvantage - For if they undertook to reap standing grain for two selas, and they reaped half of it, and [the wages of laborers] rose so that what remains to be done is worth one and a half selas, and the laborers reneged — he gives them only half a sela, because he will have to give one and a half selas to reap its second half; and this is in accordance with Rabbi Dosa. And if the employer reneges, he is at a disadvantage — Rashi explained [this as referring to a case] where [the wages of] laborers fell, and the [remaining] half is worth only a shekel [i.e., half a sela], and the employer reneged: he must give them one and a half selas, because for the [remaining] half sela he will find [others] who will finish his reaping. And [Rashi] did not want to explain that "he is at a disadvantage" [refers to a case] where [the wages of] laborers rose, such that he must give them one and a half selas for the half that they did, according to what it is worth now; for this is not logical, because why should the employer give them more than what he stipulated with them, since they lose nothing by the employer's retraction? On the contrary, they gain more, for now they will find [someone] who will give them one and a half selas to reap half [a field of] standing grain, whereas he was only going to give them one sela! And if you ask: As [the Gemara] says below (Bava Metzia 77a): "The Master said: Or they may finish their work and take two selas. [That is] obvious! No, it is necessary [for a case] where work became cheaper, and the employer retracted, and the laborers appeased him" — now, why does the employer retract in this [case] because the work became cheaper? What does he gain by retracting? Surely he must give them one and a half selas for what they [already] did! And as for the laborers too, why did they appease [him], since they lose nothing? One can answer: That the employer retracts out of animosity, because there was a quarrel between them, and the laborers appeased [him] so that they would not need to search and find [another] place to earn wages.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:6:1.hebrew: ערב ועדים אין עוברין אלא משום בל תשימון - זימנין דעברי נמי אלפני עור לא תתן מכשול, כגון שלא היה מלוה בלא ערב ועדים. אבל "לא תשימון" פסיקא ליה, אבל "לפני עור" זימנין דלא עברי, כגון שהיה מלוה לו בלאו הכי; כי היכי דמושיט כוס של יין לנזיר לא עבר אלא היכא דקאי בתרי עברי נהרא, שלא היה שותהו אם לא היה זה (ע"ז דף ו.):
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 75b:6:1.english: The guarantor and the witnesses violate only [the prohibition of]: "Do not place [interest upon him]" - Sometimes they also violate "You shall not place a stumbling block before the blind," such as where [the lender] would not have lent without a guarantor and witnesses. However, [the prohibition of] "Do not place [interest]" is categorical, whereas [regarding] "before the blind," there are times when they do not violate [it], such as where [the lender] would have lent to him even without this; just as one who hands a cup of wine to a nazirite does not violate [it] unless they are standing on two [opposite] sides of a river, such that he would not have drunk it if not for this [person] (Avodah Zarah 6a).
